stem: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly in
explanation: The resolution was moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and adopted in March 1949. It set the guiding principles for later constitutions. 1956 is the year of the first constitution.

stem: Who moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly?
explanation: Prime Minister Liaquat Ali Khan presented it on 7 March and it was passed on 12 March 1949. Jinnah had died in September 1948.

stem: According to the Objectives Resolution, sovereignty over the entire universe belongs to
explanation: The Resolution states that sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, and that authority is exercised by the people as a sacred trust. It does not vest sovereignty in an Assembly or a ruler.

stem: Which law served as Pakistan's interim constitution from 1947, with adaptations?
explanation: Pakistan adapted the 1935 Act as its working constitution until 1956. The 1919 Act was the earlier one with dyarchy.

stem: Pakistan's first constitution was enforced in
explanation: It was adopted in February and enforced on 23 March 1956. The 1962 constitution was the second and the 1973 one the third.

stem: Under the 1956 Constitution, Pakistan became
explanation: The 1956 Constitution declared the country an Islamic Republic, which is why 23 March is also remembered as Republic Day. Before that Pakistan was a Dominion.

stem: Who was the first President of Pakistan under the 1956 Constitution?
explanation: Iskander Mirza was sworn in as President in March 1956. Ghulam Muhammad had been Governor-General before the post was replaced.

stem: The 1956 Constitution adopted which system of government?
explanation: The 1956 Constitution gave a parliamentary system with a Prime Minister responsible to the National Assembly. The 1962 text was presidential.

stem: The principle of parity in the 1956 Constitution meant equal representation for
explanation: Though East Pakistan had the larger population, the Constitution gave both wings equal seats in the legislature. This was a compromise, not a division by religion.

stem: The 1956 Constitution was abrogated in October 1958 when martial law was imposed by
explanation: President Iskander Mirza abrogated the Constitution and declared martial law on 7 October 1958 and appointed Ayub Khan chief martial law administrator; Ayub removed Mirza shortly after. Bhutto came to office later.

stem: The One Unit scheme of 1955 merged
explanation: One Unit combined the provinces and states of the western wing into the single province of West Pakistan, to match East Pakistan under parity. It was dissolved in 1970.

stem: The One Unit scheme was dissolved in
explanation: West Pakistan was split into provinces again by Yahya Khan on 1 July 1970. 1973 is the year of the present constitution.

stem: The second constitution of Pakistan was enforced in
explanation: Ayub Khan announced it on 1 March 1962 and it came into force in June 1962. It was abrogated in 1969.

stem: The 1962 Constitution introduced which system?
explanation: Under the 1962 text real power lay with the President, who was both head of state and chief executive. A parliamentary system was used in 1956 and 1973.

stem: The 1962 Constitution used which indirect system for choosing the President?
explanation: Voters elected Basic Democrats, 80,000 in all, and they formed the electoral college for the President and assemblies. Adult franchise was not used for the presidency.

stem: The 1962 Constitution was abrogated in 1969 by
explanation: Ayub Khan resigned in March 1969 and handed power to General Yahya Khan, who abrogated the Constitution and imposed martial law. Zia took over in 1977.

stem: The first general elections on the basis of adult franchise in Pakistan were held in
explanation: They took place on 7 December 1970 for the National Assembly and the provincial assemblies. Earlier elections used limited franchise or indirect voting.

stem: East Pakistan became Bangladesh in
explanation: East Pakistan separated after the war of 1971 and Bangladesh emerged on 16 December 1971. The 1973 date belongs to the constitution.

stem: The Constitution of 1973 was enforced on
explanation: The National Assembly approved it on 10 April 1973 and it was enforced on 14 August 1973. 5 July 1977 is the date of Zia's martial law.

stem: Under whose leadership was the 1973 Constitution adopted?
explanation: Zulfikar Ali Bhutto led the government that brought the Constitution. He was President when it was adopted and became Prime Minister when it took effect. Chaudhry Muhammad Ali led the 1956 text; Junejo served later.

stem: What is the system of government under the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: Pakistan is a federation with a parliamentary form, where the Prime Minister heads the Cabinet. The 1962 version was presidential.

stem: The Parliament of Pakistan consists of the President, the National Assembly and the
explanation: The Majlis-e-Shoora is bicameral, with a lower House and an upper House, the Senate. Courts are part of the judiciary, not the legislature.

stem: Which House represents the provinces equally?
explanation: Every province has the same number of Senate seats, which protects smaller provinces. Seats in the National Assembly depend on population.

stem: In which House do money bills begin?
explanation: Money bills must start in the National Assembly, which controls federal finance. The Senate can only make recommendations.

stem: What is the term of the National Assembly, unless dissolved earlier?
explanation: The Assembly sits for five years from its first meeting. A six-year term is that of a Senator.

stem: What is the term of a member of the Senate?
explanation: Senators serve six years, and half retire every three years. The National Assembly, not the Senate, has a five-year term.

stem: Who presides over the sittings of the National Assembly?
explanation: The Speaker is elected by the members to preside over sittings. The Prime Minister is the head of government and answers to the House.

stem: Who is the head of state of Pakistan under the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: The President is the head of state and acts mostly on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister is chief executive.

stem: The President is elected by which group?
options: An electoral college of Parliament and provincial assemblies
explanation: The members of the Senate, National Assembly and provincial assemblies form the college. People do not elect the President directly.

stem: What is the term of the President?
explanation: The President holds office for five years. A Senator's term is six years and has no link to it.

stem: Who appoints the Governor of a province?
explanation: The Governor is appointed by the President, usually on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Chief Minister heads the elected provincial government.

stem: Who heads the government of a province?
explanation: The Chief Minister leads the provincial cabinet while the Governor is the federal representative. The Speaker presides over the assembly.

stem: The Federal Shariat Court was established to examine whether laws are
explanation: It decides whether a law conflicts with the injunctions of Islam. It was set up in 1980, and its work differs from that of the Supreme Court.

stem: The Council of Islamic Ideology is a body that
options: advises on Islamic compatibility of laws
explanation: The Council advises Parliament and the provinces on whether laws agree with Islamic teaching. It does not make laws, try cases or conduct elections.

stem: Under the Constitution, the national language of Pakistan is
explanation: Article 251 declares Urdu as the national language. English is the official language until arrangements are made for Urdu.

stem: According to Article 2 of the Constitution, the state religion is
explanation: Article 2 declares Islam as the State religion of Pakistan. Democracy and federalism are principles of government, not religions.

stem: The Constitution declares which of these as an official name of the country?
explanation: Article 1 gives the name Islamic Republic of Pakistan. The 1962 Constitution had used only Republic of Pakistan at first.

stem: Which constitutional body conducts elections in Pakistan?
explanation: The Election Commission, headed by the Chief Election Commissioner, organises elections. The Public Service Commission recruits civil servants.

stem: Which body is mainly responsible for distribution of federal revenues among the provinces?
explanation: The NFC makes awards on sharing divisible tax revenue between the federation and provinces. The Council of Common Interests settles other inter-provincial issues.

stem: The Council of Common Interests is formed under which article of the 1973 Constitution?
explanation: Article 153 sets up the Council to settle questions between the federation and the provinces. Article 251 deals with language and Article 8 with fundamental rights.

stem: Article 8 of the Constitution states that any law inconsistent with fundamental rights is
explanation: Laws that take away fundamental rights are void to that extent. They do not need a vote of the Senate.

stem: High Courts have power to issue writs under which Article?
explanation: Article 199 gives the High Courts writ jurisdiction. Article 184 relates to the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, and Article 6 to high treason.

stem: Which Article of the 1973 Constitution deals with high treason?
explanation: Article 6 makes abrogation or subversion of the Constitution high treason. Article 25 deals with equality of citizens.

stem: Which Amendment of 2010 reduced federal powers by abolishing the Concurrent List?
explanation: The Eighteenth Amendment transferred many subjects to the provinces and renamed the NWFP as Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The Eighth belonged to the Zia era.

stem: What is the minimum age for a person to vote in elections in Pakistan?
explanation: A citizen who is eighteen years old and registered on the roll may vote. 25 is the minimum age to stand for the National Assembly.

stem: What is the minimum age for a person to contest an election to the National Assembly?
explanation: The National Assembly requires candidates to be at least 25. The Senate and the Presidency need higher ages.

stem: The minimum age for election as President is
explanation: Article 41 sets the minimum age for President at 45. A person must also be a Muslim and qualified to be elected to the Assembly.

stem: Fundamental rights in the 1973 Constitution are listed in which Part?
explanation: Part II, Chapter 1, lists the fundamental rights, and Chapter 2 sets out the Principles of Policy. Part I is introductory.

stem: A bill passed by one House and rejected by the other is resolved by
explanation: When the Houses disagree, a joint sitting under Article 70 decides by a majority of the members present. Courts and referenda do not decide.

stem: Which wing's language was recognised along with Urdu as a state language in the 1956 Constitution?
explanation: Bengali was recognised as a state language with Urdu in 1956, a result of the language movement in East Pakistan. English was an official language.

stem: In which year did the Governor-General dissolve the first Constituent Assembly?
explanation: Ghulam Muhammad dissolved it in October 1954, which led to the Tamizuddin Khan case. 1956 was when the first constitution came.

stem: Who presided over the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan on 11 August 1947 after being elected?
explanation: Jinnah became its first president. Tamizuddin Khan later became its president but not at the first sitting.
